sections.overview: Scinax constrictus is a small hylid frog known from central Brazil, especially the Cerrado region.
sections.identification: Its name refers to a narrow skin fold across the shoulders; adults also have a pointed snout and small tubercles on the eyelids and jaw.
sections.habitat: It is associated with open landscapes and calls from shrubs beside permanent ponds.
sections.diet: The species-specific sources consulted do not describe its adult diet in detail.
sections.behavior: Males call with the head pointed downward from marginal shrubs during the breeding period.
sections.reproduction: Reproductive activity was observed from December to March; the original description recorded a clutch of dark eggs.
sections.ecology: The original description places it in the Scinax rostratus group and distinguishes its call and morphology from the similar Scinax nebulosus.
sections.conservation: Brazil’s 2018 Red Book records a Least Concern assessment from 2012; this is a dated assessment rather than a current population estimate.
